legend: Lincoln's Ghost Train (Hudson Valley, New York, April 1865 funeral train legend)
lines: Every April, along the Hudson River, people wait by the tracks in the dark.
They say Lincoln's funeral train still comes, the one that carried him home in 1865.
Legend says the clocks stop as it nears, and the air turns freezing cold.
A pale engine glides in, draped in black, with no driver at the controls.
A ghostly band plays a slow, muffled march.
Soldiers stand on the open cars, still as statues, pale as bone.
Then it fades into the mist, without a whistle, without a sound.
And the clocks start ticking again, as if nothing happened.
Would you wait by the tracks to see it?
title: The Ghost Train That Still Rolls Every April #shorts
description:
New York legend says Abraham Lincoln's funeral train returns every April, a pale engine, a ghostly band, and clocks that stop as it passes.
